subject: Platform barbell headcount proposal — Q4 runtime & infra
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Platform barbell headcount proposal — Q4 runtime & infra

Team —

Context and ask up front: I'm proposing a 'barbell' hiring approach for the runtime/platform org for Q4. We want to split the request into two parallel tracks to reduce operational risk and keep delivery velocity:

- Core capacity hires (2 FTE): senior Platform SREs focused on autoscaling, incident MTTR, and paging fatigue reduction.
- Strategic investment hires (2 FTE): senior Platform Engineers (inference/runtime) to own compilation/kernel selection and batching improvements.

Total ask: 4 headcount for Q4 (two Sr SREs, two Sr Platform SWEs). Budget impact is outlined in the attached 2028_Q4_runtime_hc_budget.xlsx; summary below.

Why now: we are seeing a 32% growth in peak token-throughput month-over-month and sustained paging incidents that add manual toil. The barbell model lets us shore up runbook/oncall capacity while also investing in high-leverage infra work that should reduce per-token cost.

Comp bands and suggested offers (proposed):
- Sr Platform SRE — level 5: target band midpoint $220k base + equity band C, typical total comp ~ $320k.
- Sr Platform Engineer — level 5: target band midpoint $225k base + equity band C, typical total comp ~ $330k.

If we get approval, recruiting will open reqs with a 6–8 week interview and offer pipeline. I've attached a candidate slate PDF the recruiters provided as a placeholder and a nominal budget workbook.

Immediate asks for this thread:
1) Approval to convert these budgeted seats from 'deferred' to 'open' for Q4.
2) Sign-off on comp band midpoint ranges or guidance on any exceptions.
3) Agreement on oncall compensation uplift (I propose a $12k/year oncall stipend for the SREs).

Notes: I've looped Jordan for exec visibility — if you want me to present the proposal in Friday's exec sync I'll schedule a 10-minute slot.

Thanks —
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Platform (runtime & infra)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2028_Q4_runtime_hc_budget.xlsx (Excel), platform_barbell_candidate_slate.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Platform barbell headcount proposal — Q4 runtime & infra

Grace —

Thanks for the clear framing. A few rapid questions before I take this to finance for budget conversion:

1) Can you break down the hit to run-rate vs one-time ramp hiring costs in the workbook? I need to show the quarterly cadence for run-rate impact.
2) For the comp bands: do we expect any band-exception approvals? The band midpoints you listed are above several recent platform hires — if we expect to offer above midpoint we need approver names included.
3) The oncall stipend is fine, but we should consider a differential for people taking primary rotation (I suggest $15k for primary, $7k for secondary).

If you can respond to 1–3 I can fast-track this to finance and legal for the standard SLAs and offer letter language.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
VP, Talent & Total Rewards
Redwood Inference

Grace / Kim —

Championing the request from infra/ops perspective. Two operational points:

- Paging: we are at a point where adding two senior SREs materially reduces weekly oncall load per person and should cut major incident MTTR by >20% if paired with the automation work we already scoped. That alone justifies the SRE hires.
- Cost savings runway: the two Platform SWEs will be billed to an optimization bucket and are expected to deliver batching/kv-cache gains that lower per-token spend ~6–9% over 12 months. We should hold a milestone payment (internal) tied to measurable throughput/cost KPIs.

One ask: can we designate one of the Platform SWE reqs as a 'technical lead' hire so the candidate slate prioritizes people with systems/compilers experience? If so, provide updated JD and I will make time to interview early.

Marcus
